papers.title: Theta-frequency subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation selectively improves visual attention in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: In 39 Parkinson's disease patients with bilateral STN-DBS, theta-frequency (5 Hz) stimulation improved accuracy in a visual attentional capture task and enhanced P300 amplitude exclusively in those with pre-existing visual attention deficits, while high-frequency (130 Hz) stimulation reduced accuracy and suppressed P300. No stimulation effects were observed in patients with normal attention.

papers.title: Non-invasive preoperative prediction of surgical outcomes in drug-resistant epilepsy using seizure-related EEG network dynamics.
papers.summary: The study developed a non-invasive computational framework using EEG source imaging to predict surgical outcomes in drug-resistant epilepsy by analyzing seizure-related brain network reorganization. Features derived from the presumed epileptogenic zone achieved a maximum AUC of 0.936 and 86.0% accuracy in predicting postoperative outcomes.

papers.title: Fathers, not mothers: the male singing voice and the preterm brain's response to song in the NICU.
papers.summary: In a registered trial with preterm infants in the NICU, EEG delta-band power during a sung lullaby was highest for the father's voice and male voices overall, contradicting the pre-registered hypothesis of maternal voice dominance. The results suggest that singer's biological sex, rather than maternal kinship, drives preterm cortical responses to song.

papers.title: A subject-specific mechanistic model of affect links electroencephalography, cardiorespiratory feedback, and monoaminergic dynamics.
papers.summary: The paper presents a subject-specific computational model linking EEG-derived cortical activity and cardiorespiratory dynamics to subjective affect via putative monoaminergic processes. In cross-validation on the AMIGOS dataset, the model predicted arousal with a mean RMSE of 0.380 ± 0.288, while valence prediction was more variable (RMSE 1.283 ± 1.512), highlighting the need for subject-specific modeling.

papers.title: HD-tACS at 40 Hz Improves Consciousness and Brain Connectivity in Prolonged Disorders of Consciousness: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized sham-controlled trial with 60 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness, five days of 40 Hz HD-tACS improved Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores and EEG connectivity compared to 4 Hz or sham stimulation, with 37.5% of the 40 Hz group achieving a good outcome at six months. Higher baseline 40 Hz auditory steady-state response predicted stronger network enhancement and clinical improvement.

papers.title: Concurrent observation and physical practice facilitates early closed motor skill learning: evidence from EEG source functional connectivity and behavioral performance.
papers.summary: This study tested an integrated Action Observation Training-Neuroplasticity Theory framework comparing motor observation alone versus concurrent observation and physical practice during early learning of 24-Style Tai Chi. Concurrent practice produced stronger source-level EEG functional connectivity in frontoparietal networks, better motor performance, and stronger positive brain-behavior correlations, supporting the neurobehavioral advantage of integrating physical practice into action observation for closed motor skill learning.

papers.title: Resting-state frontal theta/beta ratio and psychological symptoms in college students: an EEG study.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG was recorded from 222 undergraduate students to examine whether frontal theta/beta ratio relates to multidimensional psychological symptoms measured by the Symptom Checklist-90. Students with higher psychological symptom severity had greater frontal theta and beta power and higher theta/beta ratio, which positively correlated with total SCL-90 scores and several symptom dimensions.

papers.title: Haemodynamic and neurophysiological assessments for 2-year outcome prediction in neonates with hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis included 37 studies (n=2721) to evaluate the prognostic accuracy of amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG), cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy (cNIRS), and targeted neonatal echocardiography for 2-year neurodevelopmental outcomes or death in neonates with hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia. Abnormal aEEG background at 36 hours reliably predicted adverse outcomes (sensitivity 0.83, specificity 0.88, AUC 0.88), and cNIRS showed potential complementary value, while evidence for targeted neonatal echocardiography alone was limited.

papers.title: Cognitive state dependent enhancement of cognitive control with transcranial magnetic stimulation.
papers.summary: In 23 participants, this study tested whether rTMS effects on cognitive control depend on the cognitive state during stimulation, comparing rTMS concurrent with a high-demand cognitive control task versus a low-demand perceptual task. rTMS enhanced downstream behavioral measures of cognitive control only when delivered during the cognitive control task, and TMS-EEG showed enhanced TMS-evoked theta activity during the cognitive control task, indicating state-dependent effects.

papers.title: Sensory gamma entrainment in older adults with or without cognitive impairment: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of eight studies examined sensory gamma entrainment (GENUS) in older adults with or without cognitive impairment, including Alzheimer's disease. Findings were directionally favorable across structural, functional, biomarker, electrophysiological, and cognitive domains, including possible attenuation of hippocampal atrophy and supported target engagement, but exploratory pooled effects were not robust and cognitive benefits were not consistently established.

papers.title: The neural architecture of first-person moral choice: A demand-dependent working model.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates neuroimaging and electrophysiological evidence to propose a network-informed temporal working model of first-person moral choice, organized around integrative demand. The model distinguishes salience-related orienting, posterior default-mode/medial-temporal self-relevant situation construction, executive-control/frontoparietal comparison, and ventromedial-prefrontal value integration as flexible, interacting contributions rather than a fixed cascade.

papers.title: TMS-Evoked Cortical Reactivity Signatures as a Multidimensional Biomarker of Depression: A TMS-EEG Meta-Analysis from Diagnosis to Prognosis.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 TMS-EEG studies (1,025 MDD patients, 517 controls) found enhanced negative-polarity cortical reactivity components in MDD, particularly N100, which was associated with greater symptom severity. Treatment attenuated N100 and increased P180, and treatment-induced reduction in negative-polarity responses was strongly coupled with clinical remission.

papers.title: Scn1a-mediated developmental regulation of prefrontal cortex plasticity and cognition.
papers.summary: Using conditional expression of a mutant human SCN1A variant in adult mouse medial prefrontal cortex, this study found that adult Nav1.1 dysfunction induced epileptic activity and depressive-like behaviors but preserved mPFC-dependent cognition, unlike adolescent dysfunction. Adult dysfunction reduced sleep-related delta mPFC power and dorsal hippocampus-mPFC coherence but did not impair long-term potentiation at cortical L2/3-L2/3 prelimbic synapses, revealing a developmental role for Nav1.1 in mPFC plasticity and cognition.

papers.title: Feasibility and Usability of Home-Based Visual Evoked Potential Electroencephalogram in Neurological Telemonitoring Research.
papers.summary: This study evaluated the feasibility and usability of a home-based visual evoked potential EEG (VEP-EEG) system for migraine telemonitoring in two groups of 20 participants each. Both setups scored high on the System Usability Scale (median 91.2 and 81.2) and had similar successful electrode connection rates, supporting the feasibility of home-based VEP-EEG telemonitoring while noting the need for further signal quality validation.

papers.title: Neurocognitive mechanisms of source credibility: how work experience and patient ratings modulate the processing of medical veracity cues.
papers.summary: EEG was recorded from 36 participants evaluating true and false medical headlines paired with fictional doctor profiles varying in expertise and patient ratings. False veracity cues elicited a stronger FRN/RewP-like response when delivered by highly rated doctors, and patient ratings had a stronger effect than work experience on persuasiveness, suggesting source credibility modulates neurocognitive processing of medical veracity cues.

papers.title: AMGFM: A multimodal fusion model for depression identification based on adversarial metric learning.
papers.summary: The paper proposes AMGFM, an adversarial-metric graph fusion model for multimodal depression identification that aligns EEG, eye movement, and pupil dynamics via adversarial and metric learning and integrates unimodal/bimodal/trimodal interactions hierarchically. AMGFM achieved up to 90.33% accuracy on EFVP and AADP datasets, outperforming unimodal and representative multimodal baselines; neutral stimuli were more discriminative and EEG served as an effective target modality for alignment.

papers.title: When the Electromyography (EMG) and the Patient Disagree: Unraveling a Motor Neuron Disease Mimic With Small-Fiber Dysfunction.
papers.summary: A case report describes a 52-year-old man with an eight-year history of muscle twitching, tremor, tightness, and asymmetric cutaneous hypersensitivity initially suggestive of diffuse motor neuron disease on EMG. Repeat evaluation revealed focal ulnar neurogenic abnormalities and left L5-S1 radiculopathy without evidence of neurodegeneration, and sudomotor testing showed reduced electrochemical skin conductance in the hands indicating small-fiber/autonomic dysfunction; symptomatic treatment with gabapentin and vitamin E yielded approximately 80% improvement after six weeks.

papers.title: Intermittent photic stimulation in routine EEG: A practical guide.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: The paper provides a practical guide for performing intermittent photic stimulation during routine EEG.

papers.title: Apoptin-Derived Peptide Alleviates Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (TLE) by Limiting Neuronal Ca2+ Overload Through the HSPA1A-AP2B1 Axis.
papers.summary: The study investigates whether an apoptin-derived peptide (B9) reduces seizure susceptibility and kainic acid-induced cognitive/molecular abnormalities via the HSPA1A-AP2B1 pathway. B9 reduced PTZ-evoked seizures, attenuated epileptiform activity, improved spatial memory, and limited neuronal Ca2+ overload by disrupting HSPA1A-AP2B1 interaction, restoring AP2B1 O-GlcNAcylation and GluA2 expression; AP2B1 knockdown abolished these effects, supporting B9 as a potential TLE therapeutic.

papers.title: A neuroeducational approach to STEM education: Integrating real-time cognitive analysis and cognitive load theory to optimize teaching and learning at universities.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: A systematic narrative review with cross-case synthesis examined peer-reviewed empirical studies (2018–2025) integrating real-time cognitive analysis tools (e.g., EEG, fNIRS, eye tracking, AI analytics) with Cognitive Load Theory in university STEM education. Synthesis indicated that real-time cognitive feedback positively influenced teaching effectiveness (d = 0.68–0.72, P < 0.01), multimodal analytics improved cognitive load estimation, and cognitively based personalization reduced cognitive load and improved motivation and knowledge acquisition.

papers.title: Hyperspectral imaging-based early stress and disease detection for sustainable crop management.
papers.summary: This review examines hyperspectral imaging for early detection of biotic and abiotic plant stress, covering spectral mechanisms across visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared regions, as well as data acquisition, calibration, preprocessing, and machine/deep learning integration for disease classification and severity quantification. It highlights the potential of HSI and AI to advance precision crop monitoring and data-driven agricultural management.

papers.title: Correction: Toward clinical translation of TMS-EEG: an integrative review of multidimensional neurophysiological measures.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published integrative review on clinical translation of TMS-EEG, addressing multidimensional neurophysiological measures; no new scientific findings are presented.

papers.title: Yes, EEG reports are often poorly written.
papers.summary: This journal article asserts that EEG reports are often poorly written, but the abstract is empty and no specific methods or results are provided.

papers.title: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with diagnostic difficulty differentiating seizures from syncope: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 6-year-old girl with recurrent transient loss of consciousness initially misdiagnosed with epilepsy, in whom treadmill exercise testing later induced bidirectional ventricular tachycardia and genetic testing identified a pathogenic RYR2 variant, confirming catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Treatment with nadolol and flecainide was initiated and she remained free of syncope and seizure-like episodes for over two years.

papers.title: Correction: Foreground, midground, and restoration: EEG and preference responses to depth-controlled rural scenes.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published study on EEG and preference responses to depth-controlled rural scenes, addressing foreground, midground, and restoration; no new scientific findings are presented.

papers.title: On the stability of Born-Infeld-regularised electroweak monopoles.
papers.journal: The European physical journal. Special topics
papers.summary: The paper studies the perturbative stability of the Cho-Maison electroweak monopole when the hypercharge kinetic term is regularised by a Born-Infeld extension, which makes the monopole energy finite. It shows that after gauge fixing and constraint elimination, the Born-Infeld deformation preserves the angular channel structure of the Maxwell theory and yields a self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville-type radial problem with positive kinetic weight, providing plausible evidence for stability and a framework for future spectral analysis.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
